cues.text: Okay, Ella. As you know, the deadline for this project is the end of the month, so we’d better plan it well.
cues.speaker: Marcus

cues.text: Yes, I’ve already been thinking along those lines, and I’ve decided we should divide this project into three phases: the Pre-phase, then Phase 1, and then Phase 2, with strict deadlines involved for each one.
cues.speaker: Ella

cues.text: Given that we have to finish this quickly, that sounds good. Tell me more.
cues.speaker: Marcus

cues.text: The Pre-phrase is the simplest. We just need to allocate a space or a place to do our planning, and this space will need to be quite big.
cues.speaker: Ella

cues.text: Sure, and we have to decide on the equipment needed as well. Remember the last project, when we didn’t have enough projectors to present our ideas? We lost lots of time there.
cues.speaker: Marcus

cues.text: Yes, that was a bad start. That’s why, after the Pre-phase is finished, I’ve allocated a mere three days for Phase One.
cues.speaker: Ella

cues.text: That will involve drawing the plans. We’ll need Jenna to help us.
cues.speaker: Marcus

cues.text: And Marco.
cues.speaker: Ella

cues.text: Yes, but not Susan. Susan is just far too busy to participate, as much as I’d like her in the team.
cues.speaker: Marcus

cues.text: Let’s just take Fred instead. He’ll do.
cues.speaker: Ella

cues.text: Sure. Fred’s not as experienced as Greg, but I agree, he’ll do fine for this job.
cues.speaker: Marcus

cues.text: Then it’s straight into Phase 2, collecting, collating, analysing, and preparing the final report.
cues.speaker: Ella

cues.text: Can we do that in five days?
cues.speaker: Marcus

cues.text: I think that’s optimistic, which is why I scheduled six.
cues.speaker: Ella

cues.text: That’s almost a week! Do we have that much time?
cues.speaker: Marcus

cues.text: We do, and with the right people, six days should see the job done.
cues.speaker: Ella

cues.text: Who are the people for this phase? Arthur and Rob, right?
cues.speaker: Marcus

cues.text: No, Arthur’s got other things to do, and Rob’s on leave, so Mike alone will be the main man on this part. He’s done it before, so it should be fine. But he may need some help with the smaller tasks. Someone who is good with detail and procedures.
cues.speaker: Ella

cues.text: Hmmm. Peter’s not free at the moment, so I can arrange Leo to chip in some time and advice. Leo’s very useful, particularly under pressure. And that’s everything sorted! Well done Ella. This report should certainly be ready in time.
cues.speaker: Marcus

cues.text: Okay, Ella, you’ve done a good job with the basic timeframe of this project, but what about specifics?
cues.speaker: Marcus

cues.text: What sort of specifics?
cues.speaker: Ella

cues.text: Well, things like information gathering. Are we going to use questionnaires like we did last time?
cues.speaker: Marcus

cues.text: I was thinking of using the Internet to ask people to give their views, but you often get such silly responses when you do that. I’m of the view that the best way to find out things is to ask people directly, so that’s what we’ll do.
cues.speaker: Ella

cues.text: Okay, but that will take longer. We’ll probably even have to do some of the work at home.
cues.speaker: Marcus

cues.text: No, I don’t think so, as long as we stay back at work for some after-hours meetings.
cues.speaker: Ella

cues.text: Well, that’s better than coming in early. No one functions well in the morning. Also, the final report will need at least two appendices.
cues.speaker: Marcus

cues.text: Not only that, we’ll have to attach a small booklet to the end, containing printouts of the relevant parts from all the foreign websites we accessed.
cues.speaker: Ella

cues.text: That will take even more time. Are you sure we can meet this deadline?
cues.speaker: Marcus

cues.text: Yep, I’ve worked it all out, and I’m confident we can do it. Phase 1 should be finished by the 5th, leaving Phase 2 to begin about the 8th or 9th. Now, there’s a public holiday on the 10th, meaning that everything should be able to be submitted on the 15th , and after that, we can relax, and celebrate on the 25th when the Design Division gives us approval to go ahead.
cues.speaker: Ella

cues.text: Hah, you’re assuming that the Design Division will approve this, and that’s not guaranteed at all.
cues.speaker: Marcus

cues.text: Oh come on Marcus, be positive. You know this should be approved—in fact, I’m even planning the celebration when this is all over.
cues.speaker: Ella

cues.text: Oh yeah, what’s on the agenda, then?
cues.speaker: Marcus

cues.text: Well, we definitely don’t want a party in the office, do we? We’ll want to get away from this place, and we’re all too busy with our own lives and families to find a mutual time free for a dinner party, so I thought we’d just buy some nice expensive gifts for everyone who participated. We can just give these to the people here in the office.
cues.speaker: Ella

cues.text: That sounds fine to me, but make sure they’re not too expensive. The Budget Department will never approve the cost.
cues.speaker: Marcus

cues.text: Don’t worry; I know how much I can get away with.
cues.speaker: Ella

cues.text: Alright. I’ll leave that with you.
cues.speaker: Marcus
